title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 73
paragraphs: After this, since Alyattes would not give up the Scythians when Cyaxares demanded them, war arose between the Lydians and the Medes that lasted five years. In those years the Medes often defeated the Lydians and the Lydians often defeated the Medes, and they fought, among other engagements, a battle by night. And as they still carried on the war with equally balanced fortune, in the sixth year a battle took place in which, when the fight had begun, it happened that day suddenly turned to night. This change of day Thales of Miletus had foretold to the Ionians, setting as its limit this very year in which the change took place. The Lydians and Medes, when they saw that night had come in place of day, ceased fighting and both became much more eager that peace should be made between them. Those who brought about the peace between them were Syennesis the Cilician and Labynetus the Babylonian. These were the men who urged them to take the oaths, and they also arranged an exchange of marriages: they determined that Alyattes should give his daughter Aryenis to Astyages, son of Cyaxares, since without the compulsion of a strong tie agreements tend not to hold firmly together. Now these nations observe the same ceremonies in the taking of oaths as the Greeks do, and in addition they make an incision in the skin of their arms and then lick up the blood, each from the other.
